notes: SHIP v1.14.458 - P0: THE SW UPDATE BUTTON NOW COMPLETES THE UPDATE. THE FAILURE, CLASSIFIED. Reported on a real installed iPhone PWA: the purple SW UPDATE control appeared at v1.14.457 and tapping it did not move the app to the new build. It is the owner's case C compounded with case F - a badge shown when no worker was actually waiting, and a reload that could be answered by a stale shell. Five faults, and they depended on each other. ONE: sw.js called skipWaiting during INSTALL, so a new worker NEVER reached the waiting state. That is the root. TWO: the app posted SKIP_WAITING only if reg.waiting existed, which after fault one was never - so the message was never sent. THREE: sw.js had NO message listener at all, so even a sent message had no receiver; the activation contract was dead on both ends. FOUR: there was NO controllerchange listener anywhere in the application - the reload was a blind setTimeout of 80 milliseconds, which on a real phone always fires before a new worker can take control. FIVE: phantom_versionFileBackstop forced the badge on a version.json mismatch alone, so SW UPDATE could appear with nothing installing and nothing waiting, and the tap had nothing to promote. A SIXTH FAULT MADE THE RELOAD ITSELF UNRELIABLE. Navigations were described as network-first, but the handler called plain fetch(event.request), which uses the DEFAULT http cache mode - and GitHub Pages serves these with a max-age. So the browser's own HTTP cache could satisfy the navigation and hand back the OLD shell while reporting success. Separately version.json was served CACHE-FIRST out of PRECACHE_URLS, which broke the very backstop meant to catch stalled detection: the app fetched it with cache no-store, but that is an HTTP-cache directive and does not bypass a service worker, so the question is there a newer build was being answered out of the old build's own cache. THE FIX IS ONE PATH. A worker now installs and WAITS. The badge may appear only when a worker is genuinely parked in waiting and a tap can promote it - phantom_swActionable is the gate, and a version mismatch now triggers reg.update to go and look rather than faking the badge. One tap calls phantom_swApplyUpdate, the single activation door that both the boot row and the header pill share; the previous byte-identical duplicate inside sw_pillTap is deleted. It posts SKIP_WAITING, sw.js promotes the waiting worker, activation fires controllerchange, and exactly ONE guarded controllerchange listener performs exactly ONE reload. Navigations fetch with cache reload so the HTTP cache cannot serve a stale shell, and version.json is network-first with a cache fallback. HONEST BUTTON STATE. The control shows UPDATING while activation is in flight and repeat taps are ignored. On failure it restores itself and says why, in a toast and a console warning. A DEFECT THE NEW SPEC CAUGHT INSIDE THIS SHIP, worth recording: the failure path called sw_pillRefresh to restore the control, but the new honesty guard refuses to paint UPDATE when nothing is waiting and also refuses to touch a pill in the busy state - so a failed activation left the pill reading UPDATING forever. The guard added to prevent dishonesty reintroduced the exact dishonesty it targeted. The busy lock is now released before the refresh. NO FIELD DATA IS TOUCHED. Application shell cache is not operational truth: spec 39 asserts the site profile and rack data survive an update attempt. No reinstall, no data clearing, no Safari cache clearing is part of the flow. RUNS: spec 39 - 7 passed on phone-webkit AND 7 on desktop-chromium. The lifecycle is automatable because chromium installs service workers, which is why 05-offline skips those tests on webkit - the harness skipping something is not the same as it needing hardware. GATES: three-stamp lockstep at .458, inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, brace balance, 0 bare LF, 0 mojibake. DEVICE-VERIFY: one test, described in BATCH-VERIFY. Note this ship repairs FUTURE updates - the device has to arrive on .458 through the old broken mechanism once.
